articles.title: Cornell rape investigation will be led by a former prosecutor in the Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs case
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — A reopened criminal investigation into gang rape allegations at Cornell University will be led by a former Manhattan federal prosecutor who oversaw high-profile sex crimes cases against music mogul Sean “Diddy” Combs and fashion executive Peter Nygård, New York Attorney General Letitia James announced on Wednesday.

articles.summary: A food bank that caters to residents in Durham Region with complex health and dietary needs is looking for a new home indoors.

articles.title: Arrests made in protests of Bloor Street bike lane removal intended to quell dissent, lawyers allege
articles.summary: Four people arrested last month during protests against the removal of Etobicoke bike lanes and their lawyers say Toronto police laid "heavy-handed criminal charges" against them to deter future protests — an allegation the police service refutes.

articles.title: Road worker dead after being struck by dump truck in Pickering: police
articles.summary: A road worker has died after being struck by a dump truck in Pickering, Ont., Monday, Durham police say.

articles.title: Toronto hoping to negotiate new deal with Ontario amid financial uncertainty
articles.summary: Fresh from her election victory, Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow is preparing to try and convince Ontario Premier Doug Ford to sign a new agreement with her city. Toronto officials are hoping for a deal with the province that includes long-term funding for city hall.

articles.title: Man dead, SIU investigating after incident at U of T Mississauga: police
articles.summary: Police say one person has been found dead and a shelter-in-place order that was issued late Monday has been lifted after officers responded to a dangerous weapons call at a University of Toronto dormitory in Mississauga.

articles.title: Hundreds of food delivery drivers protest downtown to demand dignity, fair pay from companies
articles.summary: Hundreds of delivery drivers gathered at a protest in downtown Toronto on Monday to demand that their employers provide dignity and fair pay.
